app/server.mjs:1-19 — no copy-pasted entry.server/entry.client boilerplate; relies on framework defaults, so v8.2's new default server entry came for free

app/app/routes/home.tsx:56-77 — hand-rolled URL-filter state: queryString builder + refs + two syncing effects (hydration replay at :65-72, activeElement check at :75-77) instead of <Form method="get">/useSearchParams, the documented pattern per references/framework-mode.md
app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:204-212 — same bespoke ref-syncing pattern duplicated for the game selector

app/app/routes/not-found.tsx:3-8 + app/app/routes.ts:7 — catch-all route that renders null and throws 404, duplicating what root ErrorBoundary (app/app/root.tsx:33-45) already provides for unmatched locations
app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:66-70 — versionGroupOrders() assembled per-request inside the route loader instead of living in the api module alongside the cached index
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, formatting and types are centralized so a framework or API change touches few files, and no framework internals or future flags are used. The ref-based filter/game-sync effects are the one bespoke churn surface a newer search-param API or RR upgrade would force a rewrite of.

findings.issue: Filter state is hand-rolled with refs, a manual queryString builder and two syncing effects (hydration replay + activeElement guard) instead of the framework's Form/useSearchParams primitives; the same pattern is duplicated in pokemon.tsx:204-212 for the game select.
findings.suggestion: Bind inputs to useSearchParams (or a <Form method="get"> with a debounced submit), making the URL the single source of truth and deleting the ref-syncing effects.

findings.issue: Server-side fetch has no timeout or abort signal, so a hung API server stalls SSR responses and the cached promise indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) (supported in Node 24) to fetch and evict the cache entry on abort, as is already done for rejections.

findings.issue: Catch-all route whose loader throws a 404 and whose component renders null duplicates the root ErrorBoundary's NotFound (root.tsx:47-56), which already handles both unmatched URLs and thrown 404s; readers must understand the interplay to know why the component is empty.
findings.suggestion: Either drop the catch-all and rely on the root boundary, or make the catch-all render the NotFound UI itself and keep the root boundary for genuine errors.

findings.issue: versionGroupOrders() builds an index-shaped cross-request dataset inside a route loader rather than in lib/api.server.ts alongside getIndex(), so the data-access boundary leaks into route code.
findings.suggestion: Fold version-group orders into the cached Index (or a sibling cached export in api.server.ts) so all shared API-derived state lives in one module.

findings.issue: Row keys fall back to an array index (`${row.name}-${row.level ?? ""}-${i}`), which will mis-key rows when client sorting reorders them.
findings.suggestion: Assign a stable id per row when building moveTables in the loader (e.g. method + index within the unsorted data) and key on it.

summary: This is a state-of-the-art React Router 8 app: latest framework major with typed route modules, data() 404s, React 19 title hoisting, framework defaults instead of copy-pasted boilerplate, and a lean, fully current dependency set. Data access and formatting are cleanly centralized behind a server-only module with types at every boundary. The only real aging risk is the hand-rolled ref-syncing URL-filter state in home.tsx and pokemon.tsx, plus missing fetch timeouts on the server.
